This airspace can be downgraded class G upon request by glider club with special agreement. 
Activity information available on Lille Approach and ATIS.

I would like to report missing frequencies on three sub-partitions of the LILLE TMA in your French airspace dataset (fr_asp.geojson):

LILLE TMA 14 — 2000 ft to 3500 ft — class D
LILLE TMA 15 — 2000 ft to 3500 ft — class E
LILLE TMA 16 — 3500 ft to 6500 ft — class E
These three partitions are currently published without any frequency in OpenAIP, while other LILLE TMA partitions (1, 1.1, 3, 3.1, 4, 4.1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13) do have one.

Suggested frequency: 134.825 MHz — LILLE Approche

Authoritative source: French OACI 1:500 000 VFR chart (SIA). This is the only official reference I am willing to cite for a change request. The frequency 134.825 is plainly visible in the cartouche that covers the geographic area of partitions 14, 15 and 16 (around Beauvais / north of Rouen).

Technical reasoning (for context only — not a primary source): the French eAIP exposes the LILLE Approche service as a single entity with six frequencies; each frequency is bound to a specific ATC control sector (CTL) via the Frequence.Remarque field, e.g.:

134.825 — "Secteur QR-Contrôle en TMA. Sector QR (SIV 6.1 to 6.4)"
120.275 — Sector QW (SIV 2)
126.480 — Sector QE (SIV 1)
122.060 — Sector QD (SIV 4.1/4.2)
129.360 — Sector QA (SIV 3/5)
A spatial intersection between the geometries of partitions 14, 15, 16 and the CTL volumes published in the same eAIP returns the QR sector as the dominant overlap for all three, which matches what the OACI chart shows (134.825 in that region). This is consistent with the official chart and explains the absence of ambiguity for these three sub-partitions.
